title: 3.3.18 Lab: smallest(numbers)
description: Write smallest(numbers): find the smallest number in an array, starting your running answer from the array's own first item. Practice, not graded: the checks call your function.

steps.title: Write smallest
steps.instructions: Write a function declaration called smallest that takes one parameter, numbers, an array with at least one number.

steps.title: Start from the first item
steps.instructions: Make a variable called best and set it to numbers[0], not to 0 (3.3.15). If every number in the array is above 0, starting at 0 would report a number that is not in the array.

steps.title: Walk the array and update
steps.instructions: Use a for...of loop. Whenever a number is smaller than best, set best to that number.

steps.title: Return it
steps.instructions: After the loop, return best with return. Leave the array alone.

requirements.title: smallest is defined with one parameter
requirements.description: Code defines a function named smallest with exactly one parameter. Help: 3.3.15 (Arrays and Functions)
requirements.hint: Write function smallest(numbers) { ... } with exactly that name and one name between the parentheses.

requirements.title: the running answer starts from the first item
requirements.description: smallest sets a variable to the array's first item, written as something[0]. Help: 3.3.15 (Arrays and Functions)
requirements.hint: Start the running answer from the array's own first item: let best = numbers[0];

requirements.title: smallest hands back a value with return
requirements.description: smallest contains a return statement. Help: 3.2.11 (Getting a Value Back with `return`)
requirements.hint: The answer must leave the function with return, not console.log.

requirements.title: smallest returns the smallest number in the array
requirements.description: smallest(numbers) gives back the smallest number in the array, and the array is not changed. Help: 3.3.15 (Arrays and Functions)
requirements.hint: smallest must give back a number that is really in the array, the smallest one. If you got 0 for an array of positive numbers, your running answer started at 0 instead of numbers[0]. If you got the first number, check that the loop updates it.
